== Shares and the cache ==
Shares and their cache setting:
  - appdata: cache "prefer"
  - backup: cache "no"
  - documents: cache "yes"
  - domains: cache "only"
  - isos: cache "no"
  - media: cache "no"
  - oldstuff: cache "no"
  - system: cache "prefer"
!! Data is still on the cache (4 directories). It is lost when the cache device is re-created or the boot device is reinstalled. Move it to the array first: stop the Docker and VM services, then run the mover or rsync.
     appdata on pool cache: 268 KiB; share cache setting "prefer"; the appdata directory is on the cache
     documents on pool cache: 48 KiB; share cache setting "yes" (the mover has not moved it)
     domains on pool cache: 8 KiB; share cache setting "only"; the domains directory is on the cache
     system on pool cache: 4 KiB; share cache setting "prefer"; the system directory is on the cache
Docker storage (/mnt/user/system/docker/dockerdir) is on the cache. It is not moved: images are pulled again when the containers are recreated. What does not come back is each container's writable layer, listed below.
Writable-layer size per container (state kept inside the container, not in a mapped path):

  - dbtool: 0 KiB

Fit: the data on the cache (328 KiB) fits on the array: 5.8 TiB usable of 5.8 TiB free across 3 data disks, after the largest share floor (0 KiB) is kept free on each. This compares totals; it does not check that one large file fits on one disk.

Parity disk(s): parity. Their contents are not kept: they are rewritten as parity.

== Boot device and rollback ==
Unraid boots from a USB stick (vfat). Keep the stick safe at step 11 of the migration: it is the rollback.
Rollback after Debian is installed:
  - Debian on a separate device: reinsert the stick and boot.
  - Debian on the shared NVMe (with the Unraid cache): reinsert the stick, re-create the Unraid cache, and move appdata back.

== Capture ==
Written to /boot/config/hoserva/: containers.json, networks.json, disks.ini, autostart, var.ini, smart/, capture.json and this report.
Docker files are absent when Docker was not running; the capture says so.
The capture in /boot/config/hoserva/ contains your containers' environment variables, secrets included, like the templates on the same flash. The Flash Backup zip is as sensitive as the flash itself: keep it like the flash.
